name: Hiisi Island
desc: A mysterious island shrouded in ancient forests, where worship of the Moon Goddess endures. Legends tell of the golden realm's descendants who, guided by moonlight, journeyed countless miles to finally find refuge on these shores.

imgDesc.text: "O Moon, benevolent mistress, whither dost thou lead us?"
Mortals often birth wishes from pain, and faith from wishes. Yet if faith need not always be given to illusory beings, why carve cold, silent stone into shapes from dreams and ballads?
And still the moonlight flows as ever.
"We are all tainted by sin... How could we ever hope to behold the moonlight in its purest form?"
Before completing the World Quest "Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle"
After completing the World Quest "Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle"
After completing the Selenic Chronicles "The Homebound Moon"

desc.text:
Dear Miss Aila,
I am truly sorry that I was unable to stop Miss Alia in that moment. Yet, it was through her noble sacrifice that we ultimately thwarted Rotwang and prevented the loss of countless lives. Now, I finally understand why she pretended to be my close companion. I hope to speak with you about this in greater detail when next we meet — though perhaps, by then, you will already know more about all this than I.
I shall not presume to judge, nor shall I attempt to alter your opinion of her. But I ask, if nothing else, that you allow me to honor Miss Alia's final wishes by sharing her words with you. She asked that I render all possible support to you (which I surely will. You are my benefactor, after all), and that — I relay this only as she spoke it — she hoped that you would go on to live a life of happiness and freedom.
As for the Arrow of Terpikeraunas you mentioned in your last letter, if it truly holds the power to dispel the pitch-black calamity, and if you are willing to share it with such selflessness, then on behalf of the people of Nod-Krai, please accept my deepest gratitude. Should, as you foresee, Rotwang indeed rise again from the pitch-black filth, then our successors — an order I am considering naming the "Lightkeepers," in honor of the flame you have kindled — will stand ready to vanquish the threat once more, armed with the technology you have so generously gifted us.
We can speak of the details in person whenever you are free. I understand all too well that, after Lovia's passing, the Frostmoon Scions have been left with countless matters demanding your attention.
Yours sincerely,
Solovei

...I told a lie, just like Lovia did, and just like my sister did. I said no when Mr. Solovei asked me if I felt any hate.
...But how can I put the hatred in my heart into words? How would someone as kind and sincere as he is ever understand such horrifying malice?
...No. I cannot think this way, and no one needs to know. Mr. Solovei does not need to be troubled with such trivial things. No one is obliged to bear the weight of another's suffering, which they have not experienced. And even if he truly were willing to listen, and even if his kindness were to move him to tears... what would it change? I would only end up bringing needless pain to another tender heart. In the past, the present, and the future, across the countless threads of fate that Lovia once let me glimpse by mistake, the only ones who shed tears for the misfortunes of others are kind souls who ought to be smiling instead. And since the sublunary sphere has always been one where good is repaid with cruelty, the least I could do is spare him a sorrow that does him no good.
...Once upon a time, I despised lies. Yet now, I find myself speaking them with keen intent. Maybe the [...] of the past dozen years or so has been punishment for this very moment...
...But that does not matter anymore. From the noble lady of Salt to the scions of Gurabad's jinni, there have been plenty of instances where the innocent have suffered the gravest of punishments, let alone a sinner as steeped in [...] as I am. If the silvery-white thread has already found its way around my neck, I may as well bear the weight of still more unforgivable sins by myself so that the children who remain untainted may be spared...
...What was born of the Frost Moon must return to it. All the walls, towers, fortresses, and temples must be torn down, save for the great pillar raised here by the Dragonborn, that is, the sacred sanctuary where our ancestors found refuge. Prolonged isolation and seclusion serve only to nourish fleeting ambitions and hollow delusions. Let it be reverence for nature, kindness toward outlanders, and those virtues in which none believe, and not the pride of the dead, which sets our threads apart from theirs. Only then will there never again be another Lovia... or another me.
...Decades from now, a new moon goddess will be born... Oh, the irony of it! Lovia's long and desperate quest was, in the end, for nothing. Even if [...] had borne the sacred heir as foretold, and not the man who abducted my sister... The one who should have been our sovereign would only have created even greater chaos in Snezhnaya. The birth of the new moon had nothing to do with anything she did. She could not even foresee the coming of that maiden, and nor did she know that the holy throne had never truly been broken...
...I do not know if I will live to see that moment, for my own thread is hidden from my sight. But I pray that I will not. Those tainted by sin do not deserve to witness the moon's pure light...
...In any case, people must come to believe that the new moon takes delight only in kindness, friendship, and mutual aid — that no other prayer or sacrifice will ever please our goddess. This is what they must believe, because if they do not, then no matter how noble the ideal, it will only wither and fade into the filth that lies beneath the moon...
...The threads of the gods are too bright for me to follow, and I cannot see where she is headed. But at the very least, the Frostmoon Scions, who have been redeemed in her name, must ensure that the power of choice remains hers alone. No one should ever seek repayment or reward from her, and she must never be molded into the "perfect deity" others wish her to become...
...Daughter of the Frost Moon, maiden of the new moon... May she one day behold the dream of true happiness... and may the Frost Moon never forgive my sins, for I have cursed her name more times than I can count.

To the most holy and venerable Lady Lovia:
I pen this letter to account for the tragic event that transpired earlier. You asked that I send people to welcome the holy lady, and I did exactly as you instructed. But that poor girl — alas for her great beauty! — failed to grasp the kindness behind your gesture, and seized by some terrible impulse, she took her own life on the spot. For this terrible, irreparable loss, I can offer only my prayers. I pray that your compassionate goddess may ease your sorrow and keep your noble heart from breaking, despite the weight of this grief.
Regarding the "Sampo Mill" mentioned in your last letter, I am truly grateful for your openness and trust. Like you, I remain uninitiated in the true workings of this sacred relic. Yet on this matter, we are of one mind: We must find another way to rouse this ancient relic and forge a paradise, an Elysium of enduring prosperity for the people of Nod-Krai, especially your noble kin. From this moment on, I shall dedicate myself wholly to uncovering the secrets that lie within the relic.
As for the remaining matters, both more trivial and complex, I hope to discuss them at greater length with you soon. Until then, I ask that you accept these modest gifts as a small token of my regard and a gesture of sympathy for the loss that has touched your household. Please know that I hold your noble character in the highest esteem. Even at the court of His Majesty the Belyi Tsar, it is rare to encounter a lady of such uncommon foresight and deep devotion to the greater good as yourself, not to mention one who so willingly places the well-being of the nation and her people above personal sentiment. Our positions, interests, and aspirations are most closely aligned. As such, I greatly look forward to our future joint endeavors.
Your ever-steadfast friend and ally,
Rotwang

...
According to the teachings left by the apostle of the Golden City, all matters must be governed by reason alone, untainted by sentiment, for mortal tongues cannot articulate the sacred mysteries, and frail emotion will only profane the words of the ancestors. In service of a pure and exalted ideal, for the future of the scions of the far north, [...] these actions are as justified as they are necessary.
This decree has been approved by Lovia, humble handmaiden of the Frost Moon and the [...]th Archpriestess since the fall of Hyperborea.
...
Decree CMLXIII: Alternative Plan for the Sacred Heir's Selection
(All of the content that follows has been erased and cannot be read.)

...
...In accordance with the teachings of the apostle of the Golden City, all matters concerning craftsmanship and secret rites must be recorded without the taint of personal sentiment, for mortal tongues cannot articulate the sacred mysteries, and frail emotion would only profane the words of our ancestors. Do not seek to understand what lies beyond mortal intellect. Simply recite the ancient prayers with a sincere heart so that the purity of the blessings may endure.
This decree was issued by Saredne, humble handmaiden of the Frost Moon and 13th Archpriestess since the fall of Hyperborea. It is not to be defied. In the name of the mistress of the Frost Moon, the ancient laws, once obscure and difficult to understand, are now set forth in clear and concise terms, lest the faithful falter or be led astray.
...
Decree III: Elysium and the Prophecy of the Sacred Heir
Let the children of Hyperborea guard their sacred bloodline from defilement, for the heir of Elysium is destined to one day arrive.
It is hereby forbidden to marry one's closest kin. That is to say, no union shall be permitted between blood relatives.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has committed blasphemy.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has taken the life of an innocent.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has broken its oath.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that does not bear an antlered crown.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with someone from a clan that has committed parricide.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with any person disturbed of mind.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with the descendants of the fae.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with a person not of the faith.
It is forbidden to enter into marriage with an outlander.
Marriage is a most sacred act of virtue and must be kept pure. Therefore, let no unclean act stain our bloodline.
Let no action be taken to incur the displeasure of the mistress of the Frost Moon, and let no one betray their oaths.
Whosoever enters into marriage must first obtain the permission and blessing of the Archpriestess, lest a curse befall their bloodline.
Said curse shall plague their bloodline for seven generations, and then for seven more.
Whosoever breaks this oath shall have their horns severed with a silver blade. They who have been marked thus shall be cast into the long, lightless night.
Hear now the ancient prophecy: In the fullness of time, Elysium shall come, and with it, the sovereign ordained to rule over it shall also appear.
The false sevenfold radiance of the high heavens shall fall at her feet, and the bones of the earth shall rise to follow her.
For from her shall spring union with the world, and from her shall the first great cause be rebuilt.
Let these words of wisdom find root in your heart, and neglect not the sanctity of your blessed bloodline.
...
Decree VI: Offerings to the Sampo Mill
The children of Hyperborea shall guard the sacred treasure forged by the apostle of the Golden City at all costs.
Let it be known that the relic that is the Sampo Mill is a sacred work, for its blessing yields unending gold, grain, and salt.
Only the prophesied sacred heir shall have the power to rouse the Mill, and thus bring forth an Elysium of eternal abundance for us all.
According to the revelation of our ancestors, the Mill shall be sealed within a holy sanctum to preserve it from taint and desecration until the appointed time, when the sacred heir is born at last.
All followers below the rank of priestess shall not enter the holy sanctuary wherein the Mill is sealed. Those who violate this precept shall have a curse befall their bloodline.
Said curse shall plague their bloodline for seven generations, and then for seven more.
Before sowing in spring, an offering of wheat, goat's milk, and salt must be made unto the Sampo Mill, lest famine befall you.
At least one priestess shall be designated to chant prayers to the Mill day and night, to ensure a bountiful harvest and enduring prosperity.
...
Decree X: Offering to the Arrow of Terpikeraunas
The children of Hyperborea shall revere the Arrow of Terpikeraunas without fail.
Let it be known that this relic, forged of pure light, is a bow and arrow that can pierce the manifold darkness of the frozen night.
You shall mix the sacred oils in the following manner prescribed by the rites of the ancestors:
Take up a clean silver vessel free from all dust and water, for defilement is the root of all corruption.
Take the fat of a lamb, clear and pure, and warm it over a gentle fire.
It must not be too hot, or too cool. Do not bring it to a boil.
Add sulfur, salt, sawdust, and wax in their proper order while stirring with great care.
Stir until the substances inside the vessel are of one uniform color.
The number for your counting shall be seven hours. Six you shall not count, neither count you eight,
Excepting that you should count to seven. Five and nine are right out.
Then, anoint your bow and arrows with the holy oil,
And your arrows shall snuff out the pitch-black foe, shattering them like plates of silver.

(A thick stack of papers, hidden by an unknown someone in a secret compartment inside the back cover.)
...
In accordance with the statutes laid down by [...], all matters concerning Mekhaneikos and Tekhneikos shall be recorded objectively, concisely, and untainted by personal sentiment. Thus shall we guard against the distortion of truth via subjectivity, that the knowledge we possess may be transmitted with clarity to future generations, and serve the welfare of our people to the fullest possible extent.
The contents of this document have been approved by Spargapiris of Haxathrausa. All members of the order, beginning with the executive priests, shall commit its contents to memory and observe the prescribed procedures without deviation, until the reconstruction of civilization has reached five-sevenths completion (for further details, consult Tekhneikos Manual I-330).
...
If these words have reached your eyes, let it be known that you have completed the foundational disciplines of Mekhaneikos or Tekhneikos, and are hereby elevated to the rank of executive priest. Congratulations are in order.
Regrettably, your newly acquired title is not a privilege, but a burden of duty, hardship, and silent suffering borne for this realm and the countless lives she shelters.
You are destined to offer all of your youth and your life to preserve the last embers of civilization. Yet even with your final breath, you may never behold the Frostmoon's radiant light, nor see the dawn break once more upon our beautiful homeland. For the lights of the far north have been extinguished, and countless generations are condemned to cower in darkest night. No miracle has ever graced this tainted sublunary sphere, and tears have never delivered our kin from sorrow.
Then what purpose, if any, lies in all that you shall do from this moment hence?
I suppose, then, it is for an ethereal dream. A dream of countless tomorrows, for an infinity of futures yet unborn.
Only through our blood, our tears, and our toil shall our children be granted the chance to behold the glorious era and the lost Elysium we once knew. On that day, none shall weep for suffering, nor fear hunger or cold. All beings shall love one another as brothers and sisters, and all shall dwell in joy and peace.
This shall be our final and greatest dream: That our kin shall no longer be mired in superstition and barbarism. For the hope once envisioned by gods and mortals alike, we must push forward. There is no path but through.
Sear these words into your mind before you proceed to read the assessment records and operating procedures.
Hold fast to our dream of tomorrow, and let not its light be dimmed by the dust of neglect.
— Spargapiris of Haxathrausa, Acting Archpriestess of Hyperborea
...
Protocol III: Final Evaluation on Bloodline Selection and Purification
Upon evaluation and confirmation by the Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Tekhneikos Priestess, the Seed of Life Project from the Hyperborea era —henceforth referred to as the Sacred Heir Project — has been deemed to no longer be viable within the bounds of its original planned parameters. The priest who led the project, Vinda of Hithamthrausa, has passed beyond, and the essential Tekhneikos processes and Mekhaneikos apparatuses required for its continuation were lost in the fall of Hyperborea. These include, but are not limited to:
· The process of [...] cutting and modification;
· The process of [...] creation and reconstruction;
· The [...] and [...] processes, which were of the fae;
· The adaptive [...] editing process;
· ...
The aforementioned Tekhneikos processes are, at present, irreproducible.
After due deliberation, the following alternative protocol has been deemed acceptable:
· The purification of existing [...] is to be performed through controlled artificial selection, using methods primitive and inefficient.
· The phenotypic stability of each generation shall be recorded. Then, from this data, the most suitable pairs for union shall be identified, and non-coercive means employed to persuade the parties to join in union.
· Should persuasion fail to meet the criteria detailed in Tekhneikos Manual O-90, promptly proceed to the next priority match, and continue in like fashion.
· To minimize risk of disease, the Bloodline Proximity Index of all breeding pairs shall not exceed [...]. Accordingly, no individuals shall be joined in union if they share common ancestry within five generations.
This course of action is expected to yield outcomes approaching the original objective after [...] successive generations of refinement and selection. At such time, the one prophesied, the newborn Sacred Heir, shall arise. Without the need for ritual implements, nor the forfeiture of their soul, this heir shall command the pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, and shall at last attain fusion with the World.
Note: In light of projected population growth and the limits of environmental carrying capacity, it is anticipated that the practice of widespread artificial breeding may be terminated after seven generations. Thereafter, limited intermarriage with select outlanders may then be sanctioned (details in Tekhneikos Manual I-1012). Furthermore, it is hereby affirmed that, once the continuity of civilization has been assured, the descendants of the far north shall be granted the sovereign right to determine their own destinies.
...
Protocol VI: The Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb (Sealed)
The project of constructing this supremely advanced Mekhaneikos construct was personally overseen by [...] and is not fully understood at this time. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy, which would then be released in the form of [...].
Of all the known highest-tier Mekhaneikos constructs dating to the time of Hyperborea, only the Subatomic Assembling Mass-energy Patterning Orb (hereafter referred to as the "SAMPO") has endured to the present age. Its structure remains largely intact, granting it immense symbolic significance. However, a formal evaluation by the Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess has determined that the device, in its current state, is no longer functional. The collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and cannot be replicated with existing technologies. In the absence of this module, proper activation of the SAMPO is impossible, and it is presumed that even a forced restart would fail to correctly reconfigure said device (refer to appendix for more details).
After due deliberation, it is resolved that the device shall be sealed indefinitely, with no re-evaluation of its activation viability for a period of [...] generations. All personnel without explicit authorization from the Archpriestess may not breach the seal. This will prevent unnecessary accidental damage to the device.
Note: The Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess, Ariapeithea of Massagetae, has proposed a theoretically viable bypass protocol. Namely, the controlled input of [...] Realm Energy or [...] Realm Energy (refer to Mekhaneikos Manual D-503 for the possibility of the latter) at a specific carrier frequency, which may circumvent the collaborative control module and forcibly initiate the SAMPO. Upon formal evaluation, however, the proposed method was determined to pose unacceptable safety risks, with the probability of system destabilization and ensuing [...] exceeding [...]. In light of these findings, the original decision shall stand.
...
Protocol X: The Arrow of Terpikeraunas
The subject of the project is a low-tier Mekhaneikos device of the Hyperborea era, designed to solidify [...] Realm Energy into a semi-crystalline polymeric form. Once stabilized, the material is subjected to a high-frequency [...] spiral acceleration and subsequently launched, thereby purging a designated area of [...] Realm Energy contamination.
The Acting Archpriestess and the Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess have jointly affirmed that the device's remanufacture is viable. This work shall proceed under the oversight of Senior Executive Mekhaneikos Priestess Ariapeithea of Massagetae, with the prototype device projected for completion within [...] standard quarters.
Upon completion, the prototype apparatus shall be subject to regular lubrication with ointments to prevent avoidable safety incidents. (Refer to Mekhaneikos Manual D-306 for more details.)

customize.text:
<color=#ffd780>April 26, 2025</color>
The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning their ancient civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess." However, with the arrival of the Fatui, it appears that their tranquil lives are about to fade into the realm of yesterday...

The Frostmoon Enclave is home to the indigenous inhabitants of Nod-Krai, the Frostmoon Scions, who settled on Hiisi Island around six thousand years ago. Over five hundred years ago, their home was enclosed by a golden wall, through which no one and nothing could penetrate, but now the Frostmoon Scions are open to all. The first to change the Frostmoon Scions' ways was the first Moonchanter, Aila, and now the current Moonchanter, Lauma, who both revealed the truth about the true moon to the people. When the Traveler and Paimon first traveled to Hiisi Island to visit the Frostmoon Scions, a strong wind suddenly blew at the entrance to the Frostmoon Enclave, and then the flower petals transformed into a strange kuuhenki, Luonnotar, a creature said to be born with the blessing of the Moon Goddess. According to legend, the Luonnotar brings good luck, so the Traveler and Paimon allowed it to accompany them on their journey. In truth, the Luonnotar was a fragment of the Moon Goddess Columbina's soul, an anchor she left behind from the future in the past to return to Teyvat from the moon's reflection. When Columbina was able to return from the prison, the Luonnotar merged with her, but the Moon Goddess later created a new Luonnotar, imbuing it with the memories of all their past adventures with the Traveler.

At the entrance to the Frostmoon Enclave stands a statue of the Moon Goddess, built by the first generation of Frostmoon Scions to settle on the island around six thousand years ago. Similar statues were built throughout Nod-Krai and crafted from the very finest Lunasoul Stone. This stone was not only extremely rare but also infused with kuuvahki. When the Fatui pulled several fragments of Ancient Moon's Remnants down in Nod-Krai, one fell on Hiisi Island. The Fatui first began modifying and defacing the Moon Goddess statues throughout Nod-Krai, then set out to seize the last statue in the Frostmoon Enclave and its fragment of Ancient Moon's Remnants. The Moonchanter, Lauma, refused to give up the fragments to the Fatui, even under threat of attack, and promised that if they set foot on their land with ill intent, their blood would be the border. After the Fatui had repeatedly teamed up with the Frostmoon Scions to save Nod-Krai from the Sinner, Rerir, who was trying to seize the power of kuuvahki, to retrieve the Moon Goddess, and then save Nod-Krai from the Harbinger Dottore, Harbinger Marionette invited the Moonchanter to a tea party, where she brewed herbal tea according to the traditions of the Frostmoon Scions as a sign of respect and promised not to hinder them anymore.

Throughout the Frostmoon Enclave, Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms, associated with the Moon Goddess, Kuutar, grow everywhere. By their changing patterns, the Frostmoon Scions determine the approach of Moon-Prayer Night, a traditional holiday of the Frostmoon Scions in honor of the birth of the Moon Goddess. The holiday has no fixed date and depends on the movement of the moon, as Moon-Prayer Night is when the moon is closest to Teyvat. As the moon approaches, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon, and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, considered a blessed omen. When the Frostmoon Scions learned that their beliefs were false, Moon-Prayer Night became more of a local custom than a celebration of the Moon Goddess, and has evolved into the most popular holiday in Nod-Krai, celebrated even by ordinary people. Traditionally, the Frostmoon Scions decorated themselves and their settlement with the Moon-Prayer Blossoms, sang and danced, and shared food and handicrafts with all guests. When the festival spread beyond Hiisi Island to Nasha Town, people began decorating the town for the festival, and the best Frostmoon Scions' artisans sculpted a deer statue that graced the town square.

When the Moonchanter, Lauma, was born, the people exclaimed, <color=#ffffffd9>"Behold: eyes like the moonlit tide, antlers like the crescent moon, and blood that glimmers silver as the moon's reflection..."</color> For many years, the blood of the Frostmoon Scions had been fading, so large antlers like Lauma's were rarely seen more than once every hundred years. In a cave beneath Hiisi Island, there is a special tree whose branches, like Lauma's antlers, respond to the tides of kuuvahki. She was incredibly sensitive to Moon Marrow and kuuvahki’s ebb and flow. For others, the fluctuations of kuuvahki were like a gentle tide lapping away at the shore, but for her, it was a massive tsunami crashing over her body. From birth, she was revered as the Messenger of the "Frostmoon's Emissary" and the "Moon-Tide Maiden," and the first words she learned were prayers to the Frost Moon. Her first gestures were those of sacred rituals. From the moment she was first taught to pray, those closest to her would point to the night sky and say, <color=#ffffffd9>"That, Lauma, is the Frostmoon — the last of the moons, the sole surviving truth."</color> But she felt nothing from it, and later realized that people simply couldn't determine where the tide actually came from, nor did they sense the real Moon, hidden behind the veil of the sky. She had long since realized that the Moon in the sky was not real, but she couldn't tell a single soul this and chose the path of concealment. Lauma knew too much, so she was forced to keep her loved ones in the dark, and every prayer she uttered seemed like a lie to her, but it helped her to live on. Only with time, when the Moon Goddess, Kuutar, had already returned to Hiisi Island, was Lauma able to reveal the truth about the real Moon to the Frostmoon Scions. Some were unable to accept this and left the island forever, while others began to learn to live with the new truth.

Lauma also possesses the ability to understand and communicate with animals. While this often helps her learn about events in Nod-Krai or deliver messages quickly, it can often be unbearable. Since Lauma cannot control her ability, she cannot enjoy the birdsong deep in the forest. Instead of peace and tranquility, she hears arguments about who destroyed whose nest or which part of the forest contains the best twigs. Because ordinary people cannot understand animal speech and behavior, many works on this topic use the phrase "bestial nature" with a negative connotation, while "human nature" is explored in a multifaceted manner. But for Lauma, both "human nature" and "bestial nature" are simply "nature," and everyone has their moments of courage and cowardice, greed and rage. Both humans and animals rejoice in success and mourn failure, so the Moonchanter wishes for animals and humans to communicate freely. One day, the Traveler, Paimon, and the Moon Goddess wanted to ask Lauma to help a Chic Badger whose home was being attacked by monsters. While they waited for the right moment to approach the Moonchanter unnoticed, they saw how much she did for both humans and animals, constantly helping them.

One day, a Weasel Thief and an ibis offered to help Lauma retrieve the Lunar Semblance, sealed in the Moon Mirror by the previous Moonchanter. The statue's value lay in the stories associated with it, and Moonchanter hoped to find these stories, verify them, and share them with everyone. The Weasel Thief had conducted reconnaissance beforehand and discovered that the seal contained no deadly traps, then demanded payment for her assistance. The Traveler and Paimon helped Lauma remove the seal from the Moon Mirror, as pairs of mechanisms had to be activated simultaneously in two different locations. The ibis in the sky informed Lauma of their location and the mechanism before them.

Once the Lunar Semblance statue was retrieved, the animals delivered it to the Frostmoon Scions' library, which Lauma had restored. The Moonchanter also asked the Traveler to bring her texts about the Frostmoon Scions to expand her library. After the Weasel Thief helped her obtain the statue, he wanted to join the Traveler on their journey to open all the treasure chests in the world. He even gave the Traveler a Mora coin as a token of the agreement between him and the Weasel Thieves. And if they ever became interested in the offer, all they had to do was leave some dried Lakkaberries near their pillow. After finding the Lunar Semblance, the little Weasel Thief's passion only grew, and it constantly began asking Lauma about finding new treasures. Then the Weasel Thief began digging up anything it thought valuable and bringing it to her library. Thus, the library accumulated entire deposits of petrified seeds of an ancient tree, fossilized animal bones, colorful stones, Mora deposit boxes that people buried for safekeeping, wish-boxes, letters with enclosed photographs, and much more. To avoid breaking the heart of the little Weasel Thief who had given these gifts, Lauma asked another Weasel to return the stolen items to their proper place, and sorted the rest into categories.

In the library, Priestess Ehrnrooth, recording the hymns of the Frostmoon Scions, can be found. During her tenure as priestess, she learned many stories to record. For example, one of the previous Moonchanters had a strange habit of spending two hours soaking in a nearby lake whenever she had to organize some ceremony, regardless of the season. She would say that the lake reflected the moon, and that she could enjoy the favor of its light and goddess while thus immersed, which would then help the ceremony proceed smoothly. In times when a great many ceremonies were held, she would be soaking practically every day, and the constant cold caused her severe arthritis, forcing her to retire early. Despite her premature retirement, she claimed the pain was a sign of the Moon Goddess's regard, as the moon would be covered by the clouds and disappear when it would rain, as if bidding farewell. Later, in her old age, the Frostmoon Scions had to find her an acolyte to watch her permanently and ensure that she did not risk her health further. That servant turned out to be Ehrnrooth, who had learned much from the Moonchanter and dreamed of publishing the stories she told as a book. When the current Moonchanter, Lauma, learned of Ehrnrooth's book, she approved of the idea and suggested calling it "Lost Tales of the Moonchanters."

One day, a legal consultant from Liyue with Adeptal blood in her veins, Yanfei, visited the Frostmoon Scions' library. Like Lauma, she had antlers growing on her head, which fascinated the local children. Yanfei asked to see some data and materials and promised to send them some books on the "boundaries of law" in exchange, explaining issues of law, right, and legal norms in various countries. Yanfei also told Lauma the legends of Liyue and the legend of the White Horse Adeptus, who had a strong connection with the Moon. The books of the Frostmoon Scions also spoke of a deity that once lived on the surface of the Moon.

One day, the children, Kari and Ina, picked up an injured little puffin, and Kari wanted to keep it and befriend it, but the puffin flew away after getting better. The next day, the children saw another puffin in a tree and asked it to tell the little puffin that they missed it. Since the children couldn't communicate with animals, the Moonchanter came to their aid. The bird explained that the little puffin had been locked in the house and was being scolded by its parents for being away too long, but it also longed to see them. Then the other puffin and a deer escorted the children to their friend's home so they could meet, and Lauma, in gratitude, prepared sweet fruits for them in the library. When the children followed the deer and found themselves in a forest filled with dead ends, one suddenly sat on Kari's head, then crawled into his pocket and began spinning like a top, and the boy immediately recognized it as the puffin he had saved. After the children had played enough with the birds, the deer led them home so they wouldn't get lost.

In addition to the ability to speak with animals, the Moonchanter also possesses healing blood. She keeps this ability a secret, but she has used this method of healing many times, and her hands are covered in cuts, as many Frostmoon Scions distrust medicine from the Snezhnaya. One of the followers Lauma cured was a girl, Kaarina, who had fallen ill from the influence of the kuuvahki. Lauma's blood could neutralize the kuuvahki's influence on ordinary people, but a full cure still required medicine, which the Moonchanter requested from the Curatorium of Secrets. Besides Kaarina, Lauma used her blood to heal the eyes of the Curatorium of Secrets boss, Nefer, who was injured during a fight with the Rächer of Solnari.

Not far from the library, Mirsky, a mechanic from Nasha Town who is in love with Verna, a priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, can be met. They are both fascinated by mechanisms and sometimes meet to discuss various technical matters. Mirsky decided to learn the prayers of the Frostmoon Scions so that he and Verna could pray together. He also offered to install an automatic water pump, support pillars to strengthen houses, sewing machines, and make jumping frogs for children for the Moonchanter. In exchange for payment, the mechanic wanted permission to visit the library and study kuuvahki. Besides Mirsky, another Nasha Town resident in the Enclave, the carpenter Wecksell, can be met. The Frostmoon Scions once helped him, so he felt obligated and began repairing the house to pay for their help. The priestesses invited him to join the Frostmoon Scions and officially settle there, but he declined, as he didn't believe in the gods and didn't want to cause trouble. The Moonchanter, upon learning of the offer, assured Wecksell that the question of faith would not cause any concern, as he was already a member of their family.

In the caves beneath the Frostmoon Enclave, where the Frostmoon Scions left their Moon Mirrors, dwells the Tsar Crab, a mutated lord of the crabs whose mind, infected by ancient Moon Marrow, was temporarily consumed by madness. Believed to be several hundred years old, its home is an unusual shell, a huge, mountain-like structure covered in kuuvahki-filled moss. In the darkness of the cave, this moss glows like a scattering of tiny stars. Crabs around Hiisi Island often bring the Tsar Crab Lakkaberries, fish, Moonfall Silver, and other materials. According to legend, hidden in the depths of the Tsar Crab's palace is a most precious treasure,
of manipulating human desires. According to legend, the Frostmoon Scions' Archpriestess, Lovia, was also bewitched by such a stone of desire five hundred years ago, and Aila convinced the great thief Reed Miller to steal it. In reality, the stone of desire is a fragment from the orbital positioning
that recently fell on Hiisi Island. Under the influence of this fragment, the Tsar Crab learned to pass through the mirrors of the Frostmoon Scions and transformed into an evil, cruel, and hot-tempered crab, even occasionally attacking smaller crabs. The self-proclaimed heir of the great thief, Maite Veliu of the Conch Gang, set out to retrieve the Tsar Crab's treasure. The con artist Hidimbi from Sumeru told her about the wishing stone and promised to sell it for a high price. When the Traveler and Paimon teamed up with Maite to retrieve this fragment, they encountered a strange priestess in a mirror reflection along the way. She recognized the Traveler as the Ruler of "Elysium" and directed them to the fragment of the "Engraving." After defeating the Tsar Crab, the fragment returned to the main "Engraving" above the Court of the First Edict, and the Tsar Crab itself finally calmed down and stopped attacking everyone around it.

One day, while wandering through the Frostmoon Enclave, the Traveler and Paimon met the daughter of the priestess Rahetar, Kasha, who was searching for beautiful stones to bribe a friend from Nasha Town. Kasha had heard a legend about a great thief and a Fae princess, in which Reed Miller charmed the princess's heart with a gem and lured her from a gilded cage. So Kasha decided that her friend would join her on their journey if she gave her a gift. The stone Kasha was searching for turned out to be one of the fragments of the ancient dragons' orbital positioning facility, and when they retrieved it, it became drawn to a huge boulder in the center of the Enclave. After the Traveler returned the stone, the boulder suddenly rose from the ground and connected with the Engraving above the Court of the First Edict. Although Kasha couldn't bribe her friend with the beautiful stone, she now had a story to tell about the floating stone. To the right of the Enclave lies a hidden trove, which can be opened with three Evermoon Seals.

On the coast of Hiisi Island, the Traveler and Paimon once encountered the best fisherman of the Frostmoon Scions, Pekkani. Pekkani hadn't been able to catch a single fish, so he asked the adventurers to study the local waters and find out what exactly was stopping the fish from biting. Three fragments of a boulder lying nearby were discovered in the water near the fisherman. After the Traveler returned all three stones to their original position, the boulder rose and merged with the Engraving. Icy pebbles can be found all along the coast of Hiisi Island. According to ancient legend, this hole once served as a refuge to which the Frost Moon led the Fae, as well as a gateway to the ethereal. In another story popular in Nasha Town, the legendary thief, Reed Miller, was surrounded when a runestone given to him by a holy lady of the Frost Moon as a token of her love allowed him to conceal himself and escape his pursuers, but the Frostmoon Scions themselves claim this is a myth. One day, the naturalist explorer, Linnea of ​​the Adventurers' Guild, went in search of the icy pebbles and met her friend from the Conch Gang, Auni, and a man named Viljami. He told how, once upon a time, during his years of wandering the seas, he heard a calling coming from nowhere. The others didn't respond, but he fell under its spell almost instantly. Only later did he realize that this call carried within it all the dreams that were never destined to reach the distant shore, a collection of regrets. Then he recklessly rushed forward, because even danger seemed like an opportunity, but the sea and its furious winds took everything from him: wealth, honor, and even family. Auni suggested that Viljami should have looked through a hole in the icy pebble to see who was calling him, and while searching for the entrance to ethereal, her head got stuck through the hole, forcing Linnea to help her.

When the Rächer of Solnari attacked Nod-Krai and the Moon Goddess, she was too weak to fight him. To regain her strength, she asked her former colleague, the Harbinger Arlecchino, to locate the Iridescent Moon Marrow. Arlecchino was the heir to the blood of the Crimson Moon dynasty, and the ancient Balemoon Bloodfire flowed through her veins. The Crimson Moon was, in truth, the Iridescent Moon, merging with the Abyss to survive the War of Funerary Flame. When Arlecchino first became a Harbinger, the Director of the Fatui Harbingers gave her a book which claimed that in the Crimson Moon era, there was an orphanage that received children from beyond the bounds of this world and subjected them to a peculiar induction ceremony. The Crimson Moon sages looked beyond this world for beings with powers that surpassed the gods — but, fearing they might lose control, they subjected these children to a process of "refinement." They made these children crawl up a fireplace and kept asking them, <color=#ffffffd9>"Have you died?" "Did you see it?"</color> until they finally admitted to having died and seen a crimson moon. The adults embraced the children who passed the ritual, telling them, <color=#ffffffd9>"Within the fireplace, you have traversed the flames between two worlds. Here and now, you are born anew."</color> Arlecchino suspected that this was their way of "branding" the children they had enrolled — leaving an indelible mark upon them so that they would forever live in the Crimson Moon's light. And the Iridescent Moon's Marrow was sealed in a special space that could only be accessed temporarily through some kind of ritual. The chimney and fireplace were merely formalities in the ritual, and the key was crossing "the flames between two worlds" — the flames that burn within the Harbinger. On the western coast of the Frostmoon Enclave, Arlecchino opened a portal leading to the space of the Crimson Moon so that Columbina could receive its power. Moreover, this same location was the site of the battle between the Moon Goddess and her friends against the Rächer of Solnari, during which they were able to send the Sinner into the moon's reflection.

To the west of the Frostmoon Enclave is the site of the "Spirit Envoy Championship," an animal tournament. The Frostmoon Scions have always advocated coexistence with nature, encouraging their followers to build positive relationships with the beasts of the wild. At the same time, to ensure their animal friends build the strength to withstand hardship and disasters, they put selected animals with whom they share a special bond through a unique sort of training. The Spirit Envoy Championship is designed to determine the strongest human-animal pair among all the tournament participants. In previous years, the competition was restricted to the Frostmoon Scions only, but in the last year, participants from all over the world were invited to participate. The Traveler and Paimon also decided to participate with their Tepetlisaurus, Aguara, whom they found as an egg in Ochkanatlan. Friends from all over the world also arrived for the tournament: Mualani from Natlan with the Koholasaurus, Mamala, Arataki Itto from Inazuma with the beetle, Crimson Staff, Haniyyah from Sumeru with the Sumpter Beast, Fluffy the Flower King, and the Adventurer's Guild advisor Linnea with the Jack Frost, Lumi. Guests from Snezhnaya also arrived for the Spirit Envoy Championship: the Snegurochka Viliana with the fox, Gorynishche, and the Augury Bird Celaeno with the Radiant Bladehorn, Haemus. Thanks to the help of their Tepetlisaurus companion, Little One, who taught Aguara how to harness the power of phlogiston, the Traveler defeated Celaeno in the tournament finals and became the winner of the Spirit Envoy Championship. Celaeno met the Radiant Bladehorn in Nod-Krai as a cub when she came with her parents to visit her sister. Haemus had lost its parents, so she took it under her wing and raised it in Snezhnaya. After the tournament, Celaeno released Haemus into the wild on Hiisi Island so it could live freely.

customize.desc:
The Wild Hunt vanishes, chaos subsides, and the boughs of the Verdant Crest fill out quietly with life.

The Moon-Prayer Night, the night when the moon draws closest to Teyvat, is drawing near.

For a land and people long fractured, there is no better balm than a delightful night of celebration.

So why don't you and I step out together into this night of joy and laughter, amidst the blooming flowers bathed in the light of the moon?

customize.name: Nod-Krai
customize.desc:
The moon-blessed land located in the northwestern regions of Teyvat.

Follow the silver thread spun by the new moon, traverse biting gales and desolate tundras as the snow-kissed lakes, fractured like mirrors, reflect their ageless, glacial radiance. The days are bitterly short, and the night stretches on like a dark, yawning maw. But even then, the light and song of the Welkin Moon will dance gently across the faces of visiting travelers. Up at ye towers, and let your lanterns blaze into the darkness! Until the day comes... when true moonlight bathes this land once more.

customize.name: Frostmoon Scions
customize.desc: The descendants of the legendary golden realm, who chose to find new homes among the mountains and forests after abandoning all civilization. The only thing they never forsook was their faith in the "Moon Goddess."

customize.name: Moon Goddesses
customize.desc: Aria, Sonnet, and Canon — three sisters and Moon Goddesses who once ruled the firmament. Columbina Hyposelenia is a Moon Goddess who was born thousands of years after the Three Moon's death.

customize.name: Moon-Prayer Night
customize.desc: A festival celebrated by the Frostmoon Scions on the day when the Moon is closest to Teyvat, and the kuuvahki of Nod-Krai reaches its peak.

customize.name: Lauma
customize.desc: A Maiden blessed by moonlight and the grove alike, hope born to the Frostmoon Scions.

customize.name: Arlecchino
customize.desc: The Fourth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as The Knave. Her real name is Peruere.

customize.name: Yanfei
customize.desc: A well-known legal adviser active in Liyue Harbor. A brilliant young lady in whose veins runs the blood of an illuminated beast.

customize.name: Linnea
customize.desc: Naturalist and Advisor to the Nod-Krai Branch of the Adventurers' Guild.

customize.name: Columbina
customize.desc: The Trilune Goddess and the former Third of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, known as Damselette. Her real name is Columbina Hyposelenia.

customize.name: Arataki Itto
customize.desc: The first and greatest head of the Arataki Gang, famed throughout Inazuma City's Hanamizaka... Wait, what? You've never heard of them? Are you trying to be funny here?

customize.name: Mualani
customize.desc: A well-known guide in Natlan who owns a watersports shop, and expert in all forms of wave-chasing.

customize.name: Jahoda
customize.desc: The Curatorium of Secrets' extremely reliable, do-it-all super employee (or so she claims).

customize.name: Aila
customize.desc: The first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, who lived 500 years ago.

customize.desc: One of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, also known as "Rächer of Solnari."

customize.name: Celaeno
customize.desc: An Augury Bird from Snezhnaya and Linnea's elder sister.

customize.name: Crab Tsar
customize.desc: Its mind infected by ancient moonlight, this ruler of crabs was plunged for a time into delirium and madness. But just as it was about to unleash its might, it suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of a thief who broke into its court, rendering it more agreeable. Even so, this crustacean suzerain yet yearns to clash pincers with strong foes, longing to triumph over opponents worthy of its full might.

customize.name: Recipe: Today's Boon
customize.desc: A detailed step-by-step recipe for making Today's Boon.

customize.name: Moonfall Silver
customize.desc:
A silver crystal as pure and pristine as moonlight. It possesses almost perfect elemental affinity.
In the legacy of the Frostmoon Scions, these crystals were born five hundred years ago alongside the Moon Maiden, and were believed by the Moonchanter at the time to be a gift from the moon, hence the name "Moonfall Silver". However, in older documents written by Snezhnayan chroniclers, the descendants of the golden realm were already using secret silver woven by the Frostmoon thousands of years in the past. The threads that connect these two tales are unclear — the only certain thing is that these crystals make excellent elemental conductors in the eyes of Nod-Krai's craftspeople.

customize.name: Frostlamp Flower
customize.desc:
A flower that resembles a candle lamp, commonly found near water. It emits a cold, simple aroma that has a calming effect.
The contrasting colors of its stamen and stem are thought to symbolize the two different types of kuuvahki, yet despite this symbolism, it is one of the few rare plants that are immune to kuuvahki's influence. As a result, the Frostmoon Scions sometimes regard it as a symbol of faithlessness and apostasy.
It is said that this strangely shaped flower first appeared at the end of the dark calamity five hundred years ago, but this claim has never been rigorously verified.

customize.name: Rainbowdrop Crystal
customize.desc:
A crystal that gives off an iridescent glow. Exceptionally tough and malleable, it has been regarded by Snezhnayan craftspeople as the best forging material since ancient times.
It is believed that when the moon's chariot was shattered, its blood-stained axle-tip fell into the earthly realm beneath the moon, transforming into an iridescent crystal. From that day on, the people of this land no longer worshipped the dead gods. The survivors who knew what the monarchs of the night died for, however, still futilely sing those long-forgotten names.

customize.name: Nocturnal Blossom
customize.desc:
A flower in two entwined colors with a strong affinity for kuuvahki. Its light fragrance and conspicuous color have made it an excellent natural dye.
Its contrasting colors are thought to symbolize the two different types of kuuvahki, so the followers of the Frostmoon Scions sometimes regard it as the Moon Maiden's blessing.
It is said that this strangely shaped flower first appeared decades after the dark calamity ended five hundred years ago, a claim widely reflected in the verses of the Frostmoon Scions, though it has never been rigorously verified.

customize.name: Icy Pebble
customize.desc:
A pebble commonly found on Nod-Krai's coasts, characterized by a naturally occurring hollow. Touching it sends a faint chill through your finger.
According to ancient legends, the hollows in these pebbles were once shelters revealed to the fae by the Frost Moon — gateways to the ethereal. In another story popular in Nasha Town, the legendary thief, Reed Miller, was surrounded when a runestone given to him by a holy lady of the Frost Moon as a token of her love allowed him to conceal himself and escape his pursuers. Naturally, the Frostmoon Scions vehemently reject this claim, as these pebbles do not display any such magical properties.

customize.name: Lakkaberry
customize.desc:
A fruit as white as pearl that tastes refreshingly sweet.
In the legends of the Frostmoon Scions, these fruits, like kuuhenki, are a gift from the Moon Maiden, a sacred symbol blessed by the new moon. Therefore, sharing and eating delicious Lakkaberries is also a form of worshipping Kuutar.
Even when not associated with the divine, their plumpness and sweetness alone are enough to awaken one's appetite.

customize.name: Luna Treasure Compass
customize.desc:
A compass that can be used in Nod-Krai to search for nearby treasures and relevant clues.
This sublunary sphere holds countless unknown treasures, waiting to be discovered by adventurers with courage or wit.

customize.name: Radiant Antler
customize.desc:
A fragment of a defeated Frostnight Herra's majestic antlers. Light and razor-sharp, it requires no sharpening to help it slice through metal armor with ease.
According to ancient tales, these beautiful, proud creatures were created by the first emissary. When Elysium fell, they made a pact with the mistress of the Frost Moon, vowing to use the primal light bestowed by the Frost Moon to cleanse the mortal world's defilement until the patron of old could return once more. Today, these legends' origins are long lost, and their veracity is impossible to prove. Yet the creatures that once walked with the light continue to watch over this land from the shadows, through the long frozen nights and withering black tide alike — none of which could cause their forms to vanish from this world.

customize.name: Evermoon Seal
customize.desc:
Collect all 3 seals to unlock the treasure vault on Hiisi Island.

You found this round, marked stone by chance while exploring. If you collect three with the same markings, you may be able to piece together a shadow of the bright moon that once illuminated the world.

customize.name: Radiant Spincrystal 162
customize.desc: This wondrous crystal contains a certain rhythm, like something beautiful woven from delicate silk. These items can be found throughout the mainland or from merchants who collect curios. The tune held within this crystal can be revivified in your Serenitea Pot using either "Euphonium Unbound: Winding" or "Euphonium Unbound: Soaring." The tune contained within this Radiant Spincrystal is a mysterious melody from Nod-Krai.

customize.name: Radiant Spincrystal 163
customize.desc: This wondrous crystal contains a certain rhythm, like something beautiful woven from delicate silk. These items can be found throughout the mainland or from merchants who collect curios. The tune held within this crystal can be revivified in your Serenitea Pot using either "Euphonium Unbound: Winding" or "Euphonium Unbound: Soaring." The tune contained within this Radiant Spincrystal is a mysterious melody from Nod-Krai.

customize.name: Frostnight Herra
customize.desc:
Proud beings that roam in the waning glow of the moon, wielding ancient powers long since tamed by the Lord of the Sky.
Legends say these graceful, mystical beasts were born in the age when the Frost Moon still turned, and, favored by the divine emissary, they would not be tainted by the light of day. Even now, among the followers of the Frost Moon, they are regarded as sacred beasts lost to this world, retreating along secret lunar paths beyond the reach of mortal eyes. Yet, as they have for countless centuries past, they still wander in the shadows of the moon, treading the boundary between two worlds, guarding the lands coveted by calamity, and watching over those who dwell within them — for this is the very oath they first swore to the apostle of the golden city.

customize.name: Crab Tsar
customize.desc: Its mind infected by ancient moonlight, this ruler of crabs was plunged for a time into delirium and madness. But just as it was about to unleash its might, it suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of a thief who broke into its court, rendering it more agreeable. Even so, this crustacean suzerain yet yearns to clash pincers with strong foes, longing to triumph over opponents worthy of its full might.

customize.name: Gleaming Charge: Frostnight Scion
customize.desc:
An elegant elemental life form that possesses immense elemental affinity. The long years have exposed it to high concentrations of Electro, resulting in its present form.
One of the manifestations with the most violent temperament, it commands steel-shattering bolts of lightning like mere servants, such that any land it passes through shall be marked as if by a marauding, thunderous calamity.
In still-extant prayers of the far north, it was born from the Frost Moon's blessings, symbolizing the pure source and the first radiance. Perhaps this is why it finds the tainting of its pale purity with the seven colors of heavenly light unbearable, thus rejecting all life that draws too close.

customize.name: Icy Crystal: Frostnight Scion
customize.desc:
An elegant elemental life form that possesses immense elemental affinity. The long years have exposed it to high concentrations of Cryo, resulting in its present form.
It is said that this entity is closest to the original form of a Frostnight Scion. It will use icy mists and crystals to set up redoubtable walls, but perhaps it does this only to separate the flawless primeval light from the world that lies beneath the moon.
In still-extant prayers of the far north, it was born from the Frost Moon's blessings, symbolizing the pure source and the first radiance. Perhaps this is why it finds the tainting of its pale purity with the seven colors of heavenly light unbearable, thus rejecting all life that draws too close.

customize.name: Radiant Antelope
customize.desc:
A beast that has undergone a unique evolution due to age-long immersion in the ancient moon's power.
Strange lightning once fell upon the land blessed by moonlight, causing once ordinary antelopes to gain the power to wield lightning. They say that some have seen a truly strange sight — antelopes standing on cliffs at the convergence of a storm, attracting bolts of lightning to temper their bodies.

customize.name: Radiant Bladehorn
customize.desc:
A beast that has undergone a unique evolution due to age-long immersion in the ancient moon's power.
It is said that in the ancient past, when these borderlands were still shrouded by the pitch-dark shadow, only the charging of the giant rhinos could return the power that makes all things turn... And this was all that was asked of them in return for the moonlight shining down its blessings.

customize.name: Radiant Lunapod
customize.desc:
A beast that has undergone a unique evolution due to age-long immersion in the ancient moon's power.
Legend has it that when the waves of calamity rolled over the land, even those animals who dwelled in the Forsaken Sea were not spared. Those who could not accept the moonlight into themselves vanished like foam, whether great sea serpents who could send waves skyward, or single-eyed monsters who once plotted to consume all things.

customize.name: Silver Fir Wood
customize.desc: Wood harvested from the Silver Fir Tree. Humans have favored this type of wood since ancient times for its wide range of uses, from crafting barrels to constructing frameworks.
